verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's own fraud tooling lets merchants create risk rules and lists, a narrow, payments-specific way of defining rules that act automatically on payment events. Webhooks and EventBridge only deliver event notifications to the merchant's own systems, so they are a developer building block, not a rules-to-actions engine. Missing for 10: a general-purpose event-to-action automation rule builder, documentation of which actions risk rules can trigger and on which events, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
